explanation: Maintain a window with distinct characters. When a character repeats, move the left edge past its previous position without moving it backward.
timeComplexity: O(n) expected time for n characters. The right boundary visits each character once; the last-occurrence lookup gives the new left boundary directly.
spaceComplexity: O(min(n, alphabet size)) auxiliary space. Last occurrences need one entry per represented character, never one entry per window.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: The window’s left boundary stays after the previous occurrence of each character in the window. Moving it to at least one past a repeated character restores distinctness without discarding any longer valid suffix ending here. Taking the largest such suffix length over every endpoint finds the global optimum.
walkthrough: For "dvdf", the second d at index 2 moves the left boundary from 0 to 1. The final window becomes "vdf", whose three characters are distinct. Return 3.
edgeCases: The answer counts a contiguous substring, not a subsequence.
The left boundary never moves backward.
